title: On the Robustness of ChatGPT in Teaching Korean Mathematics
extended_summary:
This paper examines how well ChatGPT can solve and evaluate Korean mathematics questions, with a focus on understanding the model’s robustness in a multilingual educational setting. The authors frame the work as addressing a key limitation of current large language models: strong performance in English but weaker performance in non-English mathematical contexts. They ask two questions: how accurately ChatGPT solves Korean math problems, and how effectively it can rate and categorize those questions.

The study uses a validated set of 586 Korean mathematics questions drawn from the South Korean CSAT, a high-stakes college admissions exam. ChatGPT is used in a zero-shot setting to answer the questions and to rate them on eleven criteria such as difficulty, cognitive demand, clarity, fairness, and analytical depth. The paper also conducts topic analysis and additional prompt-engineering experiments, including translation to English and use of GPT-4o and o1-preview for some incorrect items.

Results show that ChatGPT solved 66.72% of the questions correctly, with better performance on simpler, lower-marked items and worse performance on sequential and diagram-based problems. At the same time, the model’s ratings were broadly consistent with human and educational-theory expectations, suggesting it can be useful for assessment analysis and personalized learning support. The authors conclude that ChatGPT has promise in multilingual mathematics education, but improvements are needed for low-resource languages, multi-step reasoning, and visual/diagram interpretation.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a correlational/benchmarking study of a single AI model on a fixed exam dataset, with no randomized comparison to instructional alternatives. It is methodologically useful but does not meet stronger causal-evidence criteria.
impact_tier_rationale: The reported gains are mainly descriptive and context-specific, with no demonstrated classroom-level achievement effect. The model shows promise for multilingual math support and assessment analysis, but the evidence of educational impact remains indirect and modest.

interventions.use_case: Zero-shot use of ChatGPT to solve Korean CSAT mathematics questions and to rate/categorize mathematics items on eleven assessment criteria, including difficulty, cognitive demand, clarity, and analytical depth.

finding.finding_summary: ChatGPT answered 391 of 586 Korean mathematics questions correctly, for an overall accuracy of 66.72% in zero-shot evaluation. Performance was much stronger on lower-mark questions (near 100% accuracy on 2-point items) and dropped to about 50% on the most complex 4-point items, with notably poorer results on sequential and diagram-based questions.
finding.measure: Accuracy on CSAT mathematics questions; correctness by point value; performance on diagram vs non-diagram items

finding.finding_summary: ChatGPT’s item-rating outputs were reported as substantially consistent with educational theory and test-taker perspectives, suggesting utility for higher-order judgment tasks rather than direct instruction alone. The model’s predicted difficulty, cognitive demand, and analytical depth aligned with question marks and with the notion that harder questions require more advanced reasoning and longer solution time.
finding.measure: Correlation/consistency of predicted difficulty, cognitive demand, time requirement, originality/engagement, and analytical depth with question marks and human/educational expectations

finding.finding_summary: The paper found ChatGPT could classify and rate CSAT mathematics questions across eleven criteria and perform topic analysis, indicating potential to support assessment design and content analysis workflows. The authors further showed that prompt translation and GPT-4o improved correction of previously wrong answers, increasing accuracy from 66.72% to 75.09% in the best reported scenario for incorrect items, which suggests efficiency gains for multilingual problem-solving workflows.
finding.measure: Accuracy on incorrect-question repair scenarios; rating and categorization performance; topic analysis utility
finding.study_size: n=586 questions; n=195 initially incorrect items
